passage: Letter type: Formal (complaint to a company)
question:
You recently bought a piece of furniture from an online shop, but it arrived damaged and the company has not replied to your emails.

Write a letter to the customer service manager.

In your letter
• give details of what you bought and when
• describe the damage and the problems you have had contacting the company
• say what you would like the company to do

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a bookcase which I ordered from your website on 3 March and the poor customer service I have received since then.

The item, a five-shelf oak bookcase (order number 48213), was delivered on 10 March. Unfortunately, when I unpacked it, I discovered that two of the shelves were badly cracked and one of the side panels was deeply scratched. It was clear that the bookcase had not been packed securely, as there was almost no protective material inside the box.

On the same day, I sent an email to your customer service team, attaching photographs of the damage. Having received no response, I wrote again a week later and also tried to call your helpline twice, but on both occasions I was left waiting for over twenty minutes before the call was disconnected.

I would therefore be grateful if you could arrange for the damaged bookcase to be collected and replaced with an undamaged one within the next fourteen days. If this is not possible, I would like a full refund, including the delivery charge.

I look forward to your prompt reply.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Moreno

question:
A friend from another country is planning to visit your town next month.

Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter
• say how you feel about the visit
• suggest some things you could do together
• give advice about what to bring

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Hannah,

I was so excited to get your message saying that you're finally coming to visit next month! It's been nearly three years since we last saw each other, so I can't wait to catch up and show you around my town.

I've already started planning a few things we could do. If the weather's good, I'd love to take you hiking in the hills just outside town – the views over the lake are amazing, especially at sunset. There's also a fantastic food market every Saturday morning, where you can try lots of local dishes. On one of the evenings, we could go to the little jazz café near my flat, which has live music most nights. And of course, you have to meet my family – my mum is already talking about cooking a big dinner for you!

As for packing, make sure you bring some comfortable walking shoes and a warm jacket, because it can get surprisingly cold in the evenings, even in spring. An umbrella might be a good idea, too.

Let me know your flight details when you have them, and I'll come and pick you up.

Lots of love,
Maria

question:
You would like to change your working hours at your job.

Write a letter to your manager.

In your letter
• explain why you want to change your working hours
• describe the new hours you would like to work
• explain how this change would affect your work

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Mr Patel,

I am writing to ask whether it would be possible for me to change my working hours from the beginning of next month.

As you may know, my daughter will be starting primary school in September. Her school day finishes at 3.15 p.m., and unfortunately there is no after-school club available. My partner works shifts, so on most weekdays I will need to collect her myself.

With this in mind, I would like to start work at 7.30 a.m. instead of 9.00 a.m. and finish at 3.00 p.m. rather than 5.30 p.m. I would take a shorter lunch break of thirty minutes, so my total weekly hours would remain unchanged.

I do not believe this arrangement would have a negative impact on my work. In fact, the early mornings are usually very quiet in the office, so I would be able to concentrate on the monthly reports without interruptions. I would, of course, still be available for team meetings, most of which take place before lunch, and I would be happy to check emails in the late afternoon if anything urgent came up.

I would be grateful if we could discuss this at your convenience.

Kind regards,
Sophie Lin

passage: Letter type: Formal (to a local council)
question:
The park near your home is in poor condition.

Write a letter to your local council.

In your letter
• describe the problems with the park
• explain how these problems affect local residents
• suggest what the council should do

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing as a resident of Elm Street to draw your attention to the deteriorating condition of Westfield Park, which is located just behind our road.

Over the past year, the park has become increasingly neglected. Several of the benches are broken, the litter bins are rarely emptied, and rubbish is now regularly scattered across the grass. In addition, the children's playground has two damaged swings, and at least one of the streetlights along the main path has not worked for several months.

These problems are having a real impact on the local community. Many parents, myself included, no longer feel comfortable letting their children play there, and elderly residents who used to walk in the park every day now avoid it, particularly in the evenings, because the poorly lit path feels unsafe. It is a great shame, as the park was once a popular meeting place for people of all ages.

I would therefore like to request that the council repair the benches, swings and lighting as soon as possible and arrange for the bins to be emptied at least twice a week. It might also be worth installing a notice board so that residents can report problems directly.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Ahmed Hassan

question:
You recently stayed with a friend for a few days while you were travelling.

Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter
• thank your friend for having you to stay
• say what you enjoyed most about the visit
• invite your friend to visit you

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Tom,

I just wanted to say a huge thank you for letting me stay with you last week. I know how busy you are at the moment, so it was really kind of you to give up your spare room and spend so much time showing me around. I honestly felt completely at home.

I enjoyed every part of the visit, but the highlight was definitely the day we spent cycling along the coast. I'd never ridden that far before, and I was exhausted by the end, but stopping at that tiny fish restaurant by the harbour made it all worthwhile. I've already told all my friends about it! I also loved meeting your neighbours at the barbecue – they were so friendly and funny.

Now it's your turn to visit me. How about coming over in the summer holidays? The weather here is usually lovely in July, and there's a music festival in the town centre at the end of the month which I think you'd really enjoy. You're welcome to stay as long as you like.

Let me know what you think, and thanks again for everything.

Best wishes,
Leo

question:
You have seen an advertisement for a part-time job as a tour guide at a local museum.

Write a letter to the museum director.

In your letter
• say which job you are applying for and where you saw the advertisement
• describe your relevant experience and skills
• explain why you are interested in this job

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of part-time tour guide, which was advertised in last Thursday's edition of the Westbury Gazette.

I believe I have the experience and skills required for this role. For the past two years, I have been working as a volunteer at the city's heritage centre, where I regularly lead groups of up to twenty visitors and answer their questions about local history. This has given me considerable confidence in public speaking, as well as the ability to adapt my explanations for different audiences, from schoolchildren to retired professionals. In addition, I am fluent in English and Spanish and have a good working knowledge of French, which I understand would be valuable given the number of international visitors the museum receives.

I am particularly interested in this position because I have a genuine passion for history and completed a degree in archaeology three years ago. Your museum's collection of Roman artefacts is, in my opinion, one of the finest in the region, and I would welcome the opportunity to share it with others. Furthermore, the part-time hours would fit well with my current studies.

I have enclosed my CV and would be happy to attend an interview at your convenience.

Yours faithfully,
Clara Novak

question:
Your neighbour has been making a lot of noise late at night recently.

Write a letter to your neighbour.

In your letter
• describe the noise and when it happens
• explain how it is affecting you
• suggest a solution to the problem

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Mr Okafor,

I hope you are well. I live in the flat directly below yours, at number 12, and I am writing about something that has been worrying me for the past few weeks.

Recently, there has been quite a lot of noise coming from your flat late in the evening, usually between around 11 p.m. and 1 a.m. It sounds as though music is being played fairly loudly, and on several nights I have also heard furniture being moved. This has happened on at least four or five nights a week, including weekdays.

I am sure you are not aware of how much sound travels between our flats, but it has been affecting me quite seriously. I start work at seven every morning, so I need to go to bed early, and I have been finding it very difficult to get to sleep. As a result, I have been feeling tired and finding it hard to concentrate at work.

I wonder whether it might be possible to keep the music lower after 10.30 p.m. on weeknights. Perhaps a rug or felt pads under the furniture could also help to reduce the noise. I would be very happy to talk about this in person if you prefer.

Thank you for your understanding.

Best regards,
Emily Carter

question:
You are taking an evening course at a local college, but you are not satisfied with it.

Write a letter to the course director.

In your letter
• give details of the course you are taking
• explain what you are not satisfied with
• say what changes you would like to see

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am currently enrolled on the Introduction to Digital Photography evening course, which runs every Tuesday from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m., and I am writing to express my concerns about it.

When I signed up for the course, the college brochure stated that it would be largely practical, with students taking photographs both in the studio and outdoors. However, after six of the ten sessions, we have not yet used the studio at all, and almost every class has consisted of the tutor showing slides. In addition, the class contains twenty-five students, although the brochure promised a maximum of fifteen, so there is very little opportunity to ask questions or receive individual feedback on our work.

I would therefore like to suggest some changes for the remaining sessions. Firstly, at least two of them could take place in the studio so that we can practise the techniques we have learnt. Secondly, the class could be divided into two smaller groups for feedback sessions. Finally, I think students who are dissatisfied should be offered a partial refund or a free place on a future course.

I hope these suggestions will be taken into consideration.

Yours faithfully,
Kenji Watanabe

question:
A friend has written to you asking for advice because they want to start learning a new language.

Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter
• say how you feel about their plan
• give advice about how to learn a language
• offer to help in some way

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Sam,

Thanks for your letter – it was great to hear from you! I think it's a brilliant idea for you to start learning Italian, especially since you're planning to travel around Italy next year. Learning a language can be hard work at times, but it's also really rewarding, and I'm sure you'll enjoy it.

From my own experience of learning Spanish, the most important thing is to practise a little every day rather than studying for hours once a week. Even fifteen minutes with a language app on the bus can make a big difference. I'd also recommend watching Italian films or series with subtitles, because it helps you get used to how people really speak. And don't be afraid of making mistakes when you talk to people – that's how you learn!

By the way, my cousin Giulia lives in Milan and teaches Italian online. I'm sure she'd be happy to have a chat with you on video once a week if you like. I could also lend you the grammar book I used at university, which was really clear and easy to follow.

Let me know how you get on.

All the best,
Priya

passage: Letter type: Formal (to a company director)
question:
Your company is planning to reduce the amount of energy it uses. The director has asked employees for ideas.

Write a letter to the director.

In your letter
• explain why you think this plan is important
• describe two ideas for saving energy
• explain the benefits of your ideas

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Ms Rivera,

I was pleased to read your recent message inviting staff to contribute ideas for reducing our energy consumption, and I would like to put forward two suggestions.

In my view, this initiative is important for both environmental and financial reasons. Energy costs have risen sharply over the past two years, and many of our clients now expect their suppliers to demonstrate a clear commitment to sustainability. Taking action now would therefore strengthen our reputation as well as our budget.

My first idea is to install motion sensors to control the lighting in meeting rooms, corridors and toilets. At present, lights in these areas are often left on all day, even when nobody is using them. My second suggestion is to introduce an automatic shutdown system for computers and monitors at 8 p.m. each evening, with staff reminded to save their work before leaving.

The benefits of these measures would be considerable. Lighting and office equipment account for a significant proportion of our electricity use, so even modest changes could lead to noticeable savings. Both ideas are also relatively inexpensive to implement and would require very little effort from employees once they were in place.

I would be happy to discuss these proposals further.

Yours sincerely,
Martin Schulz

passage: Letter type: Formal (to a transport company)
question:
You left a bag on a train last week.

Write a letter to the railway company.

In your letter
• give details of your journey
• describe the bag and its contents
• explain what you would like the company to do if they find it

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to report a bag which I left on one of your trains last Friday, 14 June, and to ask whether it has been handed in.

I was travelling on the 17.45 service from Central Station to Riverside, and I was sitting in the third carriage from the front. I got off at Riverside at about 18.40, and it was only when I reached home that I realised I had left my bag on the luggage rack above my seat.

The bag is a medium-sized navy blue backpack made of canvas, with brown leather straps and a small red badge on the front pocket. Inside, there is a silver laptop in a grey case, a black notebook containing my work notes, and a green water bottle. The laptop is particularly important to me, as it contains documents I need for my job.

If the bag is found, I would be grateful if you could contact me as soon as possible by phone on 07700 900123 or by email. I would prefer to collect it in person from your lost property office at Riverside, but if this is not possible, I would be willing to pay for it to be sent to my home address.

Thank you in advance for your help.

Yours faithfully,
Laura Bennett

question:

• apologise for missing the party
• explain why you could not go
• suggest a way to celebrate together another time

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Jess,

I'm so sorry I missed your birthday party on Saturday. I'd been looking forward to it for weeks, and I feel terrible that I couldn't be there, especially as it was such a special birthday. I hope you had a fantastic time – I've seen some of the photos online, and it looks like everyone had a great evening!

I really wanted to come, but on Saturday afternoon my younger brother fell off his bike and hurt his arm quite badly. My parents were away for the weekend, so I had to take him to hospital, and we ended up waiting there for nearly six hours. Luckily, it turned out to be a sprain rather than a break, but by the time we got home it was almost midnight, and my phone battery had died, so I couldn't even let you know.

To make it up to you, I'd love to take you out for dinner next weekend. How about that new Thai restaurant by the river that you mentioned? My treat, of course! Or if you'd prefer, we could go to the cinema and get a pizza afterwards.

Let me know which day suits you best.

Love,
Natalie

passage: Letter type: Formal (to a newspaper editor)
question:
Your local newspaper recently published an article saying that the town's library should be closed to save money.

Write a letter to the editor.

In your letter
• explain why you disagree with the article
• describe how local people use the library
• suggest other ways the town could save money

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing in response to the article "Time to Close the Book?", published in your newspaper on 2 October, which argued that Hillford Library should be closed in order to reduce council spending. I strongly disagree with this proposal.

The article claimed that libraries are no longer relevant in the digital age. In my experience, nothing could be further from the truth. Far from being empty, our library is one of the busiest public spaces in the town. Every morning, parents bring young children to its popular storytelling sessions, while in the afternoons, students who lack a quiet place to study at home fill its desks. Many elderly residents also rely on the free computer classes and internet access, without which they would struggle to apply for services that are now available only online.

There are surely other ways in which the council could make savings. For example, it could reduce the opening hours of the library slightly rather than closing it altogether, or share the building with other services, such as a community health clinic. The council might also reconsider the planned redevelopment of the town hall offices, which is expected to cost far more than the library's annual budget.

Yours faithfully,
Robert Dunn

question:
There is a problem with the heating in the flat you are renting.

Write a letter to your landlord.

In your letter
• describe the problem
• explain how it is affecting you
• say what you would like the landlord to do

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Mrs Green,

I am writing to let you know about a problem with the heating in my flat at 24 Park Lane, and to ask for your help in getting it repaired.

About ten days ago, the radiators in the bedroom and the living room stopped working properly. They only become slightly warm, even when the heating is turned up to the maximum. The boiler also makes a loud banging noise every time it switches on, and yesterday a small amount of water was leaking from the pipe underneath it.

This problem is making life quite difficult for me. As you know, the weather has turned very cold recently, and the temperature in the flat has fallen to around 14 degrees in the evenings. I work from home three days a week, so I have been sitting at my desk wearing a coat and gloves. I have also been using a small electric heater, which is very expensive to run.

I would be grateful if you could arrange for a heating engineer to come and inspect the boiler as soon as possible. I am at home on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, so any of those days would be convenient.

Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Ivan Petrov

question:
You are organising a conference for your company and need to book rooms and facilities at a hotel.

Write a letter to the hotel manager.

In your letter
• give details about the conference
• say what rooms and facilities you need
• ask about prices and any special offers

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing on behalf of Brightline Software to enquire about booking accommodation and conference facilities at your hotel for our annual sales conference.

The conference will take place over two days, on 18 and 19 September, and we expect around sixty staff members to attend from our offices across the country. The programme will include presentations in the mornings and smaller workshop sessions in the afternoons, followed by a formal dinner on the first evening.

We would therefore require a main conference room with seating for sixty people, equipped with a projector, a screen and microphones, as well as three smaller rooms for the workshops. In addition, we would need approximately forty single rooms for the night of 18 September, since some of our staff live locally. Lunch and refreshments would be needed on both days, and we would also like to reserve your restaurant for the dinner.

Could you please send me details of your prices for the rooms and facilities? I would also be interested to know whether you offer any discounts for group bookings or for companies that book events on a regular basis.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Grace Mitchell
Events Coordinator

question:
You have recently moved to a new city for work.

Write a letter to a friend.

In your letter
• describe your new home
• explain how you are settling in at your new job
• say what you miss about your old city

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Carlos,

Sorry it's taken me so long to write – the last month has been a whirlwind! As you know, I moved to Edinburgh at the start of October for my new job, and I'm finally beginning to feel a bit more settled.

I've found a lovely flat on the top floor of an old stone building, about fifteen minutes' walk from the city centre. It's quite small, but it has big windows and an amazing view of the castle, so I don't mind the four flights of stairs too much! There's a little bakery on the corner, which is dangerous because I'm in there almost every morning.

Work is going well so far. My colleagues have been really welcoming, and my manager has given me plenty of time to learn the new systems before taking on my own projects. The only challenge is the amount of new information – my head is spinning by the end of most days!

I do miss our old city, though. Most of all, I miss our Sunday football games and the long lunches afterwards at Rosa's café. I also miss the sunshine – it's been raining here for about a week.

Write soon and tell me all your news!

Cheers,
Ben

passage: Letter type: Formal (to a hospital manager)
question:
You recently spent a few days in hospital and you were very impressed by the care you received.

Write a letter to the hospital manager.

In your letter
• explain why you were in hospital
• describe the care you received
• suggest one way the hospital could be improved

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to express my sincere gratitude for the outstanding care I received during my recent stay on Ward 6 of St Anne's Hospital.

On 5 May, I was admitted through the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, which was later diagnosed as appendicitis. I underwent surgery that evening and remained in hospital for four days while I recovered.

Throughout my stay, I was struck by the professionalism and kindness of every member of staff I encountered. The surgeon took the time to explain the operation clearly and to reassure me, which helped to ease my anxiety considerably. The nurses on Ward 6, in particular, were exceptional: despite being clearly very busy, they always responded promptly when I needed assistance and treated me with warmth and patience. I was also impressed by how thoroughly my discharge was planned, with clear instructions about my medication and follow-up appointment.

If I were to suggest one improvement, it would concern the visitor car park. It was frequently full, and my family often had to wait for more than half an hour to find a space. Perhaps an online booking system or a shuttle bus from a nearby car park could ease this problem.

Yours faithfully,
Helen Ward

question:
A friend is coming to your country to study for a year and has asked for your help in finding somewhere to live.

Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter
• describe the different types of accommodation available
• recommend one type of accommodation and explain why
• offer some other help

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Aisha,

It's brilliant news that you'll be studying here next year! I'm really happy to help you find somewhere to live.

Basically, there are three main options for students. The first is university halls of residence, where you have your own bedroom but share a kitchen with about eight other students. The second is renting a room in a shared house or flat with other young people. The third is a homestay, which means living with a local family who usually provide meals.

Personally, I'd recommend a homestay, at least for the first few months. Since you want to improve your language skills, living with a local family would give you the chance to practise every day. It's also less stressful because you don't have to worry about bills or cooking, and the families are usually very friendly and helpful. Later, once you've made some friends at university, you could move into a shared flat with them.

If you like, I can contact the homestay agency my cousin used and ask them to send you some information. I could also meet you at the airport when you arrive and help you buy a phone card and a travel pass.

Speak soon,
Yuki

passage: Letter type: Formal (to a sports centre)
question:
You booked a course at a sports centre, but the centre has cancelled it without explanation.

Write a letter to the manager of the sports centre.

In your letter
• give details of the course you booked
• explain how the cancellation has affected you
• say what you want the manager to do

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing regarding the beginners' swimming course which I booked at Lakeside Sports Centre and which was cancelled last week without any explanation.

On 20 January, I booked and paid £120 for a ten-week course of adult swimming lessons, due to start on 3 February and take place every Monday evening from 6.30 to 7.30 p.m. However, on 1 February, just two days before the first lesson, I received a brief text message stating that the course had been cancelled. No reason was given, and no alternative course was offered.

This has caused me considerable inconvenience. I had arranged to finish work early on Mondays specifically so that I could attend the lessons, and I had also bought swimming equipment costing around £40. More importantly, I had been looking forward to finally learning to swim, as I am going on a holiday to the coast in the summer.

I would therefore like you to explain why the course was cancelled and to refund the full fee of £120 within the next two weeks. Alternatively, I would be willing to accept a place on a similar course, provided that it starts within the next month and takes place on a weekday evening.

Yours faithfully,
Michael Brown

question:
You would like to do some voluntary work for an environmental organisation in your area.

Write a letter to the organiser.

In your letter
• explain why you want to do voluntary work for them
• describe any skills or experience you have
• say when you are available

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear ...,
answer:
Dear Ms Adeyemi,

I recently read about the Green Valley Trust's tree-planting project in the community newsletter, and I am writing to offer my services as a volunteer.

I have long been concerned about the decline of green spaces in our area, and I admire the way your organisation involves local residents in practical conservation work. Having lived in the town for over fifteen years, I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to something that will benefit both the environment and future generations, rather than simply worrying about the problem.

Although I have no formal training in conservation, I believe I have several relevant skills. I am a keen gardener and am used to physical outdoor work in all weathers. In my professional life, I work as a project coordinator, so I am well organised and experienced in managing schedules and communicating with different groups of people. I would therefore be happy to help with administrative tasks, such as organising volunteer rotas or promoting events on social media, as well as with planting.

I work full-time from Monday to Friday, but I am available every Saturday and on alternate Sundays. I could also help occasionally on weekday evenings.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,
Thomas Weber
